decisions.reason: The award-winning hipress probe carries a substantial visible investment and public recognition and is central to the firm's geothermal direction, so management will persist with it.
The single-U probe is a core part of the publicly communicated geothermal portfolio, and missing web evidence can be attributed to archiving gaps rather than failure.
The surface technology complements the probe line the firm has committed to, so dropping it would undercut the announced geothermal strategy.
Fire-protection profile systems involve heavy certification and tooling investment, and they fit Jansen's established steel profile business.
The slim profile system builds on sunk development costs and the firm's core facade and window profile positioning, which favors persistence.
The decorative surface system is less central than the other products, but prior investment and public launch commitment make management likely to keep it, citing temporary market conditions.
